- **The integration base.** This workplan must be on the branch you start from. If the workplan's pull request is merged, that is `origin/main`. Until then it is the workplan branch, `origin/ccr-408aaa9b-z3e4s0` (if that name is gone: `git branch -r --contains "$(git log --all --format=%H -1 -- workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md)"`). Every command in this file uses `$BASE`, set by the first line of the set-up block, and never a literal `origin/main`: on a base that lacks the workplan, a diff against `origin/main` contains the whole workplan and every gate and count is about the wrong change.
- **Tasks that must be merged to the integration base first:** T-026 merged. Check by running that task's own after-test (its section 6), or `git log "$BASE" --oneline | grep -F "<that task's commit subject>"`.
- **Owner decisions:** none outstanding. The decisions this task needed are resolved under delegation (next bullet); none is still the owner's.
- **Delegated resolutions this task rests on.** OD-03: forms table; `canonical_en` kept as our English descriptive label, never a form; the name shown derived by E1. Each is a resolution by an Opus-class model under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-12: not the owner's words, reversible by the owner, and read only through the ledger's gate (`grep -n -F "Convention 2026-11-12 — how a delegated resolution" references/project-standards.md`). Run it before you start and again before you open the pull request; if any line prints CLOSED, stop (section 9):
```
gate(){ s=$(grep -F "$1 STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1); c=$(grep -F "$1 CHECK:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1); case "$s" in *"ANSWERED BY THE OWNER"*) echo "$1 OPEN (owner)";; *"RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION"*) case "$c" in *"not required"*|*confirmed*) echo "$1 OPEN (delegated; ${c#*CHECK: })";; *) echo "$1 CLOSED (check: ${c:-none})";; esac;; *) echo "$1 CLOSED (${s:-no status line})";; esac; }
for n in OD-03; do gate $n; done
```
- **Tests that must be red (or green) before you start:** AT-25 red. (`AT-` numbers are the acceptance tests of `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/hs-improvement-programme.md` §4, §7 and §9 and of `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/td-requirements-and-interface-spec.md`; the test this task must turn is restated in full in section 6, so you do not need to open either.)

Build `tasks/T-028-design.md` (committed 2026-11-12), to the delegated resolution of OD-03 (`workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS.md`, section OD-03): a concept's identity is `terms.term_id`; its names are rows of **one** forms table, **`term_aliases`** (no `term_forms` table is built: the design's section 2 says why), rebuilt by one schema migration to one row per occurrence keyed by `form_id` (= the old `rowid`), with a unique occurrence index in place of the primary key and a nullable `usage_type` (design sections 3 and 10; the migration carries an `AFTER_DATA` marker). **Schema migration (this task has one).** Never type a migration number. Derive it at execution time: `ls scripts/migrations | grep -E '^[0-9]{3}_' | sort | tail -1` gives the highest; yours is that plus one, zero-padded, in `scripts/migrations/NNN_<slug>.sql`, and it ends by setting `PRAGMA user_version` to the same number. ## 8. Every writer that screens or matches a name, and how it changes

| Writer (locate by symbol in `scripts/db.py`) | Today | After T-028 |
|---|---|---|
| `_name_holder(conn, name, *, aliases, exclude_term)` | exact match on `canonical_en` first, then on any alias in any language | `_name_holder(conn, name, language, *, exclude_term=None)` returns **every** clash, none first: `label` (another term's `canonical_en`, case-folded, compared only when `language` is EN) and `form` (an **attested** member form in the same language, case-folded). Seeds never clash (E4); they are returned as `seed_matches` for information. |
| `_near_terms(conn, name)` | token overlap with every `canonical_en` and every EN alias | `_near_terms(conn, name, language)`: token overlap with attested member forms in `language`, and with labels only when `language` is EN. A non-English name is never screened against English. Tokenising is T-009's script-aware `_name_tokens`; until T-009 merges, a non-Latin name yields no tokens and no near match, which the refusal text must say. |
| `insert_term` / `add-term --from-observation` | mints the term and the NAMES-NEW adjudication; refuses a label not inside the observed phrase; writes no form | also writes the observation's surface form as the concept's **first member row** (`alias_type SYNONYM`, `observation_id` set, `attestation` from `--attestation instrument\|other_source`, required); screens the label as a label and the surface form as a form; the inside-the-phrase rule applies only when the observation's language is EN (section 6) |
| `add-term`, **new base route** | — | `db.py add-term --first-form "<text>" --form-language XX --form-jurisdiction YY --source-url URL (--source-page P \| --source-clause C) [--source-line N] --attestation instrument\|other_source [--usage-type T] --canonical-en "<our label>" --rationale "..." [--distinct-from TERM-ID ...] --session S`. Exactly one of `--from-observation` and `--first-form`. Writes the term and its first member row in one transaction. Refuses: a (language, jurisdiction) pair `lang_jur_map` lacks; no locator; a value-bearing label (the existing `_VALUE_BEARING_NAME` refusal); an English first form whose text does not contain the label; a label clash; an attested form clash in that language unless named by `--distinct-from` (a recorded conflation). |
| `rename_term` / `rename-term` | sets the label; writes the old label into `term_aliases` as `DEPRECATED` | sets the label; writes **no** alias row; new warrant route `--from-form <form_id>` (an attested member form of this term whose text equals the new label), beside `--from-observation` and `--ruling-quote`; label screen only |
| `mint_term_from_catalogue` | exact clash on label and aliases | label screen only (a catalogue entry is our English register, not an attested form) |

| `observe-term`, `adjudicate-term` | evidence-stage reading | unchanged (the scan contract) |

## 0. Verdict

**The plan is complete as to the owner decisions it registers, and not complete as to open items.** After the fifth set, no register decision a task waits on is CLOSED (D-27 prints nothing), D-27b prints nothing (OD-17 is deferred by the owner), and the generator reports no missing dependency, no cycle and no blocking decision:

- **A** resolvable now by a plan-document, ledger (append) or generator edit;

Canadian English. Every count is a command; where a figure is printed beside one, re-run the command and trust its output, not the figure (CLAUDE.md rule 7a)._

## 0. Verdict

**The plan is complete as to the owner decisions it registers, and not complete as to open items.** After the fifth set, no register decision a task waits on is CLOSED (D-27 prints nothing), D-27b prints nothing (OD-17 is deferred by the owner), and the generator reports no missing dependency, no cycle and no blocking decision:

```
python3 -I scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/build_batches.py | head -2
# at writing: tasks 68 batches 8 missing deps [] crit 8
#             decisions 38 blocking [] standing ['OD-17'] open 37 unregistered []
```

What is still open is listed in section 2, one row per item, each classed:

- **A** resolvable now by a plan-document, ledger (append) or generator edit;
- **B** needs a new task (tooling or research, apart, rule 10);
- **C** needs the owner;
- **D** resolvable only at execution time (a pilot, a run, a probe);
- **E** not resolvable now; accepted as a standing limit or declined, with the reason.

```

**The three findings that matter most**, in the owner's order of criteria (integrity first):

1. **`main` holds a stale copy of this workplan, and every task file would start from it** (OI-01, OI-02). PR #218 merged an earlier version; the three plan commits since, the three design files and the fifth-set ledger entry are not on `main` (`git log --oneline origin/main..origin/ccr-408aaa9b-z3e4s0`). Every task file sets `$BASE` by testing only whether `origin/main` *has* `REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md`, so it now picks `origin/main`, and T-018, T-026, T-055 and T-102 would stop on a missing design file, or worse, run on stale text. Nothing can start until the plan is merged.
2. **The prior workplan's agreement rules are carried by no task, yet T-110 writes the first live determinations** (OI-09). `workplan/2026-10-23-pipeline-resolution-workplan.md` is "DRAFT, NOT EXECUTED"; this plan imports its T-1a, T-2 and T-3 (as T-016, T-017, T-019) and replaces T-5 (by T-037), but its T-4 (the owner's rulings OR-4, OR-5 and OR-6: anchoring, Co-1 setting a value, unsatisfiable anchors recorded `divergent`), T-1b and T-8, and its data PRs, have no task here and no recorded decline. A first determination computed without the ruled agreement rules would misstate what the evidence supports. Two of the owner's own questions behind T-4 (OR-5b, OR-6c) are still open in the owner queue (OI-07).
3. **The OD-39 supersession pair, as designed, would have turned a check red** (OI-05, fixed in step 1). The audit cannot anchor a `SUPERSEDES` pair whose target is inside the ledger; tested on a scratch copy, PASS became FAIL. T-018 now records the supersession in prose.

# T-114  Retire MOVE and VES to the access needs that carry them

_One task, one pull request. Read `CLAUDE.md` first; beyond it this file is self-contained. Index, order and the owner decision register: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md`. Evidence base: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/01-handshake-ledger.md`, as corrected by `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/fa-corrections-for-suite.md` (where they differ, the corrections govern). Every number in this file was read on 2026-11-12 and is given with the command that produces it: re-run the command; do not trust the number._

**Pilot status.** Not piloted. Written in the last fold pass of 2026-11-12, from the owner's third set of answers. Three tasks of this plan were executed in scratch clones (T-006, T-008, T-010) and the defects they showed in the task files were corrected in every file by one generator; this file's own steps have not been executed by anyone. Its evidence command was run on 2026-11-12 and printed what section 3 states. Expect to find a defect in this file, and report it rather than work around it.

## 1. Identity

| | |
|---|---|
| Task | T-114 |
| Title | Retire MOVE and VES to the access needs that carry them |
| Wave | research |
| Layer (CLAUDE.md §3) | 3 |
| Kind | **RESEARCH** (CLAUDE.md rule 10: tooling and research never share a pull request) |
| Executor | Sonnet-class |
| Traces to | OD-37 (owner, 2026-11-12, third set: "MOVE and VES are access needs, agreed") |

## 2. Preconditions

- **The integration base.** This workplan must be on the branch you start from. If the workplan's pull request is merged, that is `origin/main`. Until then it is the workplan branch, `origin/ccr-408aaa9b-z3e4s0` (if that name is gone: `git branch -r --contains "$(git log --all --format=%H -1 -- workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md)"`). Every command in this file uses `$BASE`, set by the first line of the set-up block, and never a literal `origin/main`: on a base that lacks the workplan, a diff against `origin/main` contains the whole workplan and every gate and count is about the wrong change.
- **Tasks that must be merged to the integration base first:** T-054 merged (the successor column and `retire-identity`). Check by running that task's own after-test (its section 6), or `git log "$BASE" --oneline | grep -F "<that task's commit subject>"`.
- **Owner decisions that must be answered first.** The answer must be in `references/project-standards.md` (the ledger), in the owner's words.
  - **OD-37** — answered by the owner, 2026-11-12 (third set): "MOVE and VES are access needs, agreed." (`grep -n -F "OD-37: identity-lens rule" references/project-standards.md`). Check: `grep -F "OD-37 STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1` must read `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`.
- **Tests that must be red (or green) before you start:** both codes `active` with no successor.
- **Set-up.**

```
cd /home/user/guidebook
bash .claude/hooks/ensure-deps.sh && python3 -c "import pydantic, jsonschema, yaml"
git fetch origin
BASE=$(git cat-file -e origin/main:workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md 2>/dev/null && echo origin/main || echo origin/ccr-408aaa9b-z3e4s0); echo "BASE=$BASE"
git switch -c task/t-114-retire-move-ves-to-needs "$BASE"
STEM=session_$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)-<slug>            # the session stem: bare in the database, with .md for emit_data_migration --session
export SCRATCH="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/guidebook-t-114" && mkdir -p "$SCRATCH" && cp data/guidebook.db "$SCRATCH/s.db" && cp data/guidebook.db "$SCRATCH/t.db"   # s.db is the batch's working copy; t.db is for probes
```
- **Shell variables do not survive from one tool call to the next in this harness.** Write the stem down once and begin every later command block by setting `BASE`, `STEM` and `SCRATCH` again to the same values.
- **Real execution:** open with `/session-open` (it sets `scratchpad/CURRENT` to the stem and creates the folder of the same name), then `/orient`. Follow `skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md`. **Pilot or dry run** (a scratch clone): skip `/session-open`, stay on the branch you were given, do the work on the scratch copy only, and stop before the write path below.
- Work only on the scratch copy and point every call at it inline:
```
GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$SCRATCH/s.db" python3 scripts/db.py <verb> ... --session "$STEM"
```
- Land the rows only by the write path, after the work is finished:
```
python3 scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py --scratch "$SCRATCH/s.db" --out "$SCRATCH/batch.sql"
python3 scripts/emit_data_migration.py --session "$STEM.md" --summary "<what the batch is>" --input "$SCRATCH/batch.sql"
python3 scripts/migrate_db.py
python3 scripts/migrate_db.py --rebuild "$SCRATCH/rebuilt.db"      # must exit 0
```
Research batches are serial: if another research batch merged after you copied the database, `emit_batch_sql.py` refuses ("copied from a different base"). Do not force it; start again from the new base.

## 3. The problem, in the guidebook's terms

The owner agreed that movement disorders and vestibular disorders are access needs, not identity populations. The registry still lists them as identities.

**Evidence command** (read-only):

```
python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(c.execute(\"select identity_code,status,superseded_by_need from base_taxonomy_identity where identity_code in ('MOVE','VES')\").fetchall())"
python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);T=[t for (t,) in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table'\")];print({t+'.'+r[1]:c.execute('select count(*) from \"'+t+'\" where \"'+r[1]+'\" in (?,?)',('MOVE','VES')).fetchone()[0] for t in T for r in c.execute('pragma table_info(\"'+t+'\")') if r[1] in ('identity_code','target_population','pop_a','pop_b','parent_code')})"
```

**Expected output today (after T-054):** both `active`, no successor; 0 rows of either code in every identity-bearing column. If any live row carries either, it is re-tagged first (section 4, item 1).

## 4. The change

Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect.

1. If any live row carries `MOVE` or `VES` (the second evidence command), re-tag it by judgment through the sanctioned lens writers: its need (`A-PRECISION` for a movement disorder, `A-STABLE` for a vestibular one), and the medical lens where the source names a diagnosis. Never copy the figure. If no writer can change that row's lens, stop: a writer gap for its own tooling pull request.
2. `retire-identity --code MOVE --need A-PRECISION` and `retire-identity --code VES --need A-STABLE`, each with the ledger pointer to the OD-37 answer and a reason quoting it.
3. Do not touch `MH`, `NDV` or `TALL` (retained by the owner) or `ALL`, `DEAF`, `LMB`, `COM` (unchanged unless the owner says otherwise).

**What reads what this task adds or changes:** every writer that takes an identity code (they now refuse the two codes and name the need); the lens switch.

**Data migration.** This task lands rows through `scripts/emit_data_migration.py`, which names the file itself; never type a migration name or number. The pull request contains no schema migration.

## 5. Caller sweep

A research task renames nothing and changes no code, so the sweep that applies is the one for prose that restates a fact your rows change (CLAUDE.md rule 7a). For each row id, code or value you change, search the reading surface and the governance prose, and correct a sentence your rows make false (or stop, if correcting it is not research):

```
V='<the id, code or value you changed>'
git grep -n -F -e "$V" -- governance architecture CLAUDE.md references skills ':(exclude)references/project-standards.md' ':(exclude)references/search-log'
```

Structures this task touches, for orientation: `MOVE`, `VES`. The ledger (`references/project-standards.md`), `sessions/` and committed migrations are records and are never edited.

## 6. Verification

**Red before, green after.** Before: both `active`. After, on the migrated database: `select identity_code,status,superseded_by_need from base_taxonomy_identity where identity_code in ('MOVE','VES')` prints `('MOVE', 'deprecated', 'A-PRECISION')` and `('VES', 'deprecated', 'A-STABLE')`, and the second evidence command prints 0 for every column.

**Fixtures.** Probes run on `$SCRATCH/t.db`; the batch's own rows are written on `$SCRATCH/s.db` and reach `data/guidebook.db` only through the write path of section 2.

**The gates, once each:**

```
BASE=$(git cat-file -e origin/main:workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md 2>/dev/null && echo origin/main || echo origin/ccr-408aaa9b-z3e4s0)
python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --session "$STEM" > "$SCRATCH/dod.txt" 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; grep -E 'EXAMINED|BLOCKED|PASS|FAIL' "$SCRATCH/dod.txt" | tail -8   # the research gate
scripts/preflight.sh --base "$BASE" --explain > "$SCRATCH/gate.txt" 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; grep -E '^(RESULT|PREFLIGHT|SELFTEST)|FAIL|NOTHING-IN-SCOPE' "$SCRATCH/gate.txt"
```
- **Run each once, after the migration is applied and before the commit.** `preflight.sh` runs the selftest and `run_checks.py --changed-from`; do not run `run_checks.py` separately, and never `--all`.
- **Proof that each gate examined something.** A check scoped to a session id that matches no row passes having read nothing. Confirm the stem is the one stored on your rows. The tables a batch writes carry `created_by_session` and `updated_by_session`; for each table this task writes, `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3,sys;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(c.execute('select count(*) from '+sys.argv[2]+' where created_by_session=? or updated_by_session=?',(sys.argv[1],sys.argv[1])).fetchone())" "$STEM" <table>` must be above 0 after the migration is applied. `research_batch_dod` prints its own `EXAMINED:` lines: read them in `dod.txt`. A passing check prints no `EXAMINED:` line in `gate.txt`; any check under `NOTHING-IN-SCOPE` there has not passed. `migration_reproducibility` compares row counts only, so an UPDATE is invisible to it: also run `python3 scripts/audit/migration_reproducibility.py --deep`, which compares every row.

## 7. Commit

Commit **after** the gate of section 6 is clean.
```
git add -A . ':!transcripts' ':!*commands.jsonl'      # add the two append-only logs only at a natural break (CLAUDE.md rule 6)
git commit -m "run-pipeline: retire MOVE and VES to the access needs that carry them [$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')]" -m "<body: what changed, the evidence commands and their output, the callers the sweep found and what was done to each>" -m "<the attribution trailers your own session instructions give: a Co-Authored-By line and a Claude-Session line>"
```
The format is `{skill-name}: {action} [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM]`, timestamp last, taken from `date -u`. Do not copy trailers from this file; use the ones your session was given.

## 8. What you must NOT do

- Do not write `data/guidebook.db` directly. Rows land only by the write path of section 2.
- Do not hand-write SQL against a table a `db.py` verb can reach. A table no verb reaches is a gap to file (`db.py add-gap`), not a licence.
- Do not put tooling in this pull request: no schema migration, no new verb, no new check, no edit under `scripts/`, `schemas/`, `.github/` or `skills/` (CLAUDE.md rule 10). A writer gap found on the way is filed and left.
- Do not write a bibliographic field from memory when a payload is in hand; do not mark a source verified that was not re-retrieved; never leave `verification_status` NULL.
- Do not move, round or re-key an adjudicated figure. Do not back-translate a term. Do not delete an empty search.
- Do not author `best_practice_synthesis` or synthesis prose below the Opus floor.
- Do not decide doctrine (mission, audience, CRPD posture, population taxonomy, evidence-tier definitions, jurisdiction scope, licensing, trajectory). Stop instead.
- Do not treat any `[A-Z]-NN` code as a container, an example or a name.
- Do not run `scripts/run_checks.py --all`, `scripts/bootstrap.sh`, or `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Do not push to `main`, rebase or force-push. Do not subscribe to pull-request activity or schedule check-ins.
- Do not hand-type a count into any file or message; write the command that computes it.

## 9. Stop conditions

Stop, change nothing further, and report (what you ran, what you saw, what you expected) when any of these happens:
- a precondition in section 2 is not met, or an owner decision named there is unanswered or answered in another form;
- the evidence command in section 3 does not give today's expected output (the defect may already be fixed, or the ground has moved);
- the red test is not red before the change, or is not green after it, after one honest attempt;
- the sweep of section 5 finds a caller (as defined there) that you cannot repair without adding something section 4 does not name. A caller you can repair is repaired and listed; a mention is left;
- a check or test that was green in the before-run is red in the after-run, at any level (the test files are registered as advisory, so the gate will not stop you: the before-and-after comparison is what does);

content.content:
## Owner clarification 2026-11-12 (ninth set) — the lower-limb child of MOB is LLD, "people with lower-limb differences", not PROSTH

Given by the owner in answer to the prompt "Rename PROSTH" (put to them because, after `LMB` became `UPL` and left mobility, "PROSTH" read as any prosthesis user). Recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. The owner selected the option's label: "LLD — 'people with lower-limb differences'".

**What this settles.** The lower-limb child of `MOB` is **`LLD`, people with lower-limb differences**, replacing the proposed `PROSTH`. It is defined by the condition (a lower-limb difference), not by the device, so it holds people who use a lower-limb prosthesis and people with a lower-limb difference who use none. It is the lower-limb counterpart of `UPL` (upper limb, outside mobility). The mobility family is therefore the parent `MOB` with the children `WHEEL` (which takes in `SCI`), `LLD` and `WALKAID`. This departs, for this one child, from the owner's earlier decomposition "by device" (wheelchair user, prosthetic device user, other mobility aids); the owner chose it knowing so.

**What it does not decide.** (1) That a lower-limb prosthesis is a device and is held in `device_class` (the T-102 design proposed adding `lower_limb_prosthesis`, `crutches` and `cane`): with `LLD` defined by the condition, whether the prosthesis value remains in `device_class` as a descriptor of a figure or participants is for the design to restate, keeping one home per fact. (2) The registry description of `LLD`. (3) Whether the old `LMB` rows' lower-limb content goes to `LLD` and its upper-limb content to `UPL`: `LMB` was described as "people with limb differences; upper-limb disabilities", and the owner has made `LMB` into `UPL`; the 6 identity–ICF map rows on `LMB` (as of 2026-11-12) have to be placed on `UPL` or `LLD` by what each names. [ASSUMPTION: the identity codes are not mutually exclusive, so a person with a lower-limb difference who also uses a wheelchair or walking aid is in `LLD` and in `WHEEL` or `WALKAID`; unratified.]

OI-13: the lower-limb child of MOB is LLD, people with lower-limb differences (replacing PROSTH); the mobility family is MOB with WHEEL (taking in SCI), LLD and WALKAID; LMB becomes UPL outside mobility
OI-13 STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER

CONDITION: any session writing the mobility family's registry rows, or tagging a figure that names a lower-limb difference, a prosthesis, a wheelchair or another aid.
ACTION: (1) Use `LLD`, not `PROSTH`. (2) Place the rows of the old `LMB` on `UPL` or `LLD` by what each names. (3) Keep the prosthesis, where it is a device fact, in `device_class` only if the design settles it there without a second home. (4) Treat the [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified. This supersedes the confirmed T-102 code `PROSTH` (fifth set) and the seventh set's pairing of `LMB` with `PROSTH`.
DATE: 2026-11-12 — owner clarification (selected option), quoted above.
